cases.title: A/R Detail lists the five buckets in fixed order and rows by name
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure the report has open documents in all five aging buckets on today's date.
  • Make sure that in the "1-30 days past due" bucket, customer A has one open invoice, invoice A, and customer B has two, invoice B and invoice C. Customer B's name comes first alphabetically, and invoice B's number is smaller than invoice C's but has fewer digits.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. On the report page, read the bucket rows from top to bottom without expanding anything.
  2. Look at the header of the "Customer Full Name" column.
  3. Click the chevron of the "1-30 days past due" bucket to expand it.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The buckets read, in this order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current".

Step 2:

  • "Customer Full Name" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 3:

  • The bucket opens and shows its rows: customer B's two invoices come first, invoice B above invoice C (smaller number first, counted as a number), then customer A's invoice A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-p-aging-detail-opens-by-vendor-name.png: figure "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-p-aging-detail-as-it-opens-today.png: figure "A/P Aging Detail as it opens today" (Production (before)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "Buckets stay in fixed order; rows inside each bucket go by vendor name (was most overdue first). S1-R5, S2-R4, S2-R5." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name")
  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Inside a bucket, rows open most overdue first. No sortable headers." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail as it opens today")

cases.title: A/R Collection groups customers by name, rows oldest date first
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have two customers with overdue invoices on today's date: customer A and customer B; customer B's name comes first alphabetically.
  • Make sure customer B has three overdue invoices: invoice A with the oldest date, and invoice B and invoice C with the same later date. Invoice B's number is smaller than invoice C's but has fewer digits, and invoice C was invoiced earlier that day than invoice B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Find the groups of customer A and customer B and note their order.
  2. Look at the header of the "Date" column.
  3. Expand customer B's group.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer B's group is above customer A's group.

Step 2:

  • "Date" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 3:

  • The group opens: invoice A first (oldest date), then invoice B, then invoice C: on the same date the smaller number comes first, counted as a number, whatever the time of day each was invoiced.


· If you see exactly that, mark this test FAILED and do not raise anything new.

· If it fails in a DIFFERENT way from what is described above, that is a NEW problem — please report it.

· If it PASSES, the fix has shipped: report it so the ticket can be closed and this note removed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S1-R6: “A/R Collection groups by customer and A/P Unpaid Invoices by vendor, groups in name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4); inside each group, rows open oldest date first; rows on the same date, whatever the time of day they were created, go in document-number order (S2-R4).”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.


References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-p-aging-detail-opens-by-vendor-name.png: figure "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Buckets stay in fixed order; rows inside each bucket go by vendor name (was most overdue first). S1-R5, S2-R4, S2-R5." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name")

Difference from the PRD (DD-04), closed: PRD version 5 said "inside each group, rows open oldest date first, ties by document number (S2-R4)" (S1-R6); the design shows in the CMLZ Truck Repair - Talladega group five invoices dated Aug 27, 2026 read S3-14690, S3-14693, S3-15660, S3-14691, S3-14692 (not number order). Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answers 12 and 14): document-number order, as the PRD says, whatever the time of day the invoices were created. The build bug is ticket SV-12138, and the design (5 Nov 2026) keeps the picture with the caption "Known build bug: invoices on the same date show in time-of-day order here; the PRD puts them in invoice-number order (S1-R6)." This case follows the PRD (S1-R6, S2-R4, unchanged in version 11). The held design-version case D-79 (C715561) was deleted from TestRail on 26 Oct 2026 with the QA lead's go-ahead (snapshot in v9-pass-2026-10-26/deleted/).

cases.title: A customer with nothing open on the as-of date is not listed
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer, customer A, with no open documents: its only invoice is paid in full.
  • Have a customer, customer B, with one open invoice, created today, and nothing before today.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Look for customer A and customer B in the list.
  2. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer A is not listed, as today.
  • Customer B is listed.

Step 2:

  • The report reloads for yesterday.
  • Customer B is not listed: on yesterday's date it had nothing open.

Preconditions

  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.

  • Leave the report with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.
cases.custom_steps:
1. Click the "ID" header.
  2. Click the "ID" header again.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header.
  4. Click the "Due Date" header again.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by ID as numbers, never letter by letter, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 2:

  • Largest number first: document C, document B, document A, still in number order.

Step 3:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by Due Date, oldest first.
  • Document A, document B and document C tie on Due Date, so they are ordered by number, smallest first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 4:

  • The Due Date sort reverses, newest first.
  • The three still tie and keep the same order, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C (reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only).

cases.title: A/R Summary: the PDF and CSV match the rows and order on screen

  • The CSV downloads.

  • The CSV holds exactly the same rows in the same order, with a "Location" column.

  • The lines read "As of Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days" (menu order, not the order ticked), then "Customers: " and customer B, customer A (the order ticked).

  • The CSV downloads.

  • The CSV starts with four rows of one line each, in this order: "As of: Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days", then "Customers: " and customer B, customer A.
  • The column heading row follows directly.
  • There is no Location column.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S3-R4: “Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).”
  • S3-R5: “Each export states the locations under the as-of line: "Locations: All locations" when every location is ticked, otherwise "Locations: " followed by the ticked locations' names in the Location menu's order (A to Z), separated by a comma and a space, for example "Locations: Main Shop, North Bay". Under it, only when set: "Past due: " and the ticked ranges in menu order (for example "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days"), then, for one ticked customer or vendor, "Customer: " or "Vendor: " and the name, and for several, "Customers: " or "Vendors: " and the names in the order they were ticked.”
  • S3-R8: “The CSV starts with the lines of S3-R5, each in its own row, in this order: As of, Locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor line only when set. The column heading row follows directly, then one flat table: one row per customer or vendor (Summaries) or per document (Detail, Collection, Unpaid Invoices), with the aging bucket, customer or vendor in its own column; no group header or subtotal rows; one Totals row at the bottom. Money is a plain number with two decimals, and an empty bucket is a blank cell; dates are YYYY-MM-DD.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S6-N1: “With one location chosen, the column is hidden on screen and in the export.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”

  • Every group expands.

cases.title: A/R Detail: the group row stays pinned under the headings
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that on today's date the report has two buckets, bucket A and the next bucket below it, bucket B, each with more lines than fit on the screen.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the groups of bucket A and bucket B expanded.
cases.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into bucket A's rows.
  2. Keep scrolling until bucket B's row reaches the top.
  3. Keep scrolling into bucket B's rows.
  4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside bucket A's rows again.
  5. Scroll down fast through bucket A's and bucket B's rows.
  6. Scroll fast back up through bucket B's and bucket A's rows.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Bucket A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • It shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count.
  • It shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row).

Step 2:

  • Bucket B's row pushes bucket A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Bucket B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: bucket A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Step 6:

  • The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D21: “Pinned group row = scroll-driven overlay (ReportPinnedGroupRow + useReportPinnedGroup) showing the group row's chevron and full label — on A/R Collection including "Phone:" and "Credit term:" (S9-R1/R2) — but no money cells (the group's subtotals stay in its own row)”
  • Tech plan §7 Manual testing checklist: “3. Fling-scroll a long expanded group: pinned row pushes up without overlapping header or totals.”

(or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. cases.custom_steps: 1. Read the filter row under the title, chip by chip, left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Four chips, in this order: the date chip "As of: " and today's date (for example "As of: 10/15/2026"), the Customer chip, the Past due chip, the Location chip.
  • The date chip says "As of", no longer "Date".
  • The Customer chip reads "Customer: All customers" with a person icon.
  • The Past due chip reads "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon.
  • Both are in the resting (grey) style.
  • The Location chip reads "Location: All locations" with the location pin icon.
  • Every label matches exactly, capitals and punctuation included.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S5-R6: “The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.”
  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”
  • S5-R10a: “Filter choices are not remembered between visits: opening a report from the Reports menu starts on today's as-of date, no customer or vendor, Past due Any, and All locations.”
  • What changes for existing users: “The date filter is labelled "As of" (was "Date"). On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices the Customer or Vendor chip now comes after it.”

cases.custom_preconds:

  • The page address carries "customerIds=" followed by customer A's code (a long code, not the name).

Step 2:

  • The address bar shows customer A's code, a comma and "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

Step 3:

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: " and customer A's name.
  • Only customer A's group is listed: the unknown customer is ignored.

  • The address bar shows "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: All customers" in the resting (grey) style: with no known customer left, the link opens as if none were ticked.

cases.title: A/R Collection: a report that fails to load says so in place of the rows
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Use Google Chrome (or Microsoft Edge) on a desktop: the report's data is cut off with the browser's own blocking tool. Switching Wi-Fi off does not work for this test: ShopView then sends nothing, waits for the connection and shows no message (as before this release).
  • Run it on staging. On a QA site the page shows the result for about 5 seconds, then the site's own "QA env is sleeping" notice moves it to an "Environment Sleeping" page, so only the first steps can be judged there.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Block the report's data: press F12, click the ⋮ menu at the top right of the panel that opens, choose More tools, then Network request blocking; tick "Enable network request blocking", click +, type *reporting/reports* and click Add. Leave the panel open.
  2. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
  3. Unblock it: in the Network request blocking panel, untick "Enable network request blocking".
  4. Change the as-of date back to today.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The computer is offline.

Step 2:

  • The report tries to load and fails: in place of the rows it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again.", with the standard error message as well.

Step 3:

  • The computer is online again.

Step 4:

  • The report loads normally again.


A server error cannot be caused by hand; a lost connection is the failure a tester can cause.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R6: “If a report fails to load, it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, with the standard error message.”

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Pick two as-of dates: date A, on which A/R Summary lists exactly 2,000 customers, and date B, on which it lists exactly 2,001.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Set the as-of date to date A.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Set the as-of date to date B.
  4. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • 2,000 customer rows (the Totals row is not counted).

Step 2:

  • The PDF downloads with the "Success" message.

Step 3:

  • 2,001 customer rows.

Step 4:

  • "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again.": exactly one message and no PDF downloaded (no new file in the browser's downloads).

The row count is the customers listed, not the Totals row. No test site has 2,000 customers with open invoices (the QA organization has 46), so this exact boundary is checked by the developers (SV-11595); the PDF boundary itself is checked by hand on A/P Detail.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S3-N1: “Over 2,000 rows, the PDF is refused before anything is generated: no download, and the message "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again." Exactly 2,000 rows is allowed.”
  • S3-R9: “The row count for the export limits is the number of customer or vendor rows (Summaries) or document rows (the other four), not counting headers, subtotals or the Totals row.”
  • S3-N3: “A refused export shows exactly one message (S3-N1 or S3-N2), never a second generic error.”

cases.title: A/P Detail: a PDF of exactly 2,000 lines downloads, 2,001 is refused
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that today the organization has more than 2,001 open A/P lines.
  • Pick a set of vendors, the chosen vendors, whose open A/P lines today add up to exactly 2,000.
  • Have a vendor, vendor B, that is not one of the chosen vendors and has exactly one open A/P line today.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. In the Vendor filter, tick every one of the chosen vendors.
  2. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the CSV and count its document rows (leave out the heading and the Totals row).
  4. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. In the Vendor filter, also tick vendor B.
  6. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Only the lines of the ticked vendors remain.

Step 2:

  • The CSV downloads with the "Success" message.

Step 3:

  • Exactly 2,000 document rows.

Step 4:

  • After a wait (a 2,000-row PDF can take about 30 seconds), the PDF downloads with the "Success" message: exactly 2,000 rows is allowed, and bucket rows, subtotals and the Totals row are not counted.

Step 5:

  • Vendor B's line is added, so the report now has 2,001 document rows.

Step 6:

  • "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again.": exactly one message.
  • No PDF is downloaded (no new file in the browser's downloads).

The QA organization has far more than 2,000 open A/P lines, so the exact boundary is reached by ticking vendors whose lines add up to 2,000; the setup file lists them for the day of the test. If step 4 shows "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." while the CSV in step 2 worked, the test site may not have its PDF generator set up (tech plan): mark this test Blocked: "PDF generator not available on this site", not Failed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S3-R9: “The row count for the export limits is the number of customer or vendor rows (Summaries) or document rows (the other four), not counting headers, subtotals or the Totals row.”
  • S3-N1: “Over 2,000 rows, the PDF is refused before anything is generated: no download, and the message "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again." Exactly 2,000 rows is allowed.”
  • S3-N3: “A refused export shows exactly one message (S3-N1 or S3-N2), never a second generic error.”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §9 Known risks: “PDF generation: WeasyPrint HTTP (600 s client timeout) pins an FPM worker; the 2,000-row cap bounds it (~30 s).”
  • Tech plan §7 E2E backlog: “PDF generator not configured on every environment; CSV covers wiring”

cases.title: A/R Summary: the Totals row adds up every customer, not only those loaded
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that between 31 and 90 customers have open documents on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  2. Open the CSV and read its Totals row.
  3. Switch back to the report and read its Totals row.
  4. Scroll down until the next customers load.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 2:

  • Note the Totals row's Total (it adds up every row of the report).

Step 3:

  • The screen's Totals row reads the same Total as the CSV's: it adds up every customer, not only the 30 loaded so far.

Step 4:

  • The Totals row reads the same after more load.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S3-R3: “The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.”
  • S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. There are no page buttons. A/R Detail and A/P Detail show each bucket's first 100 lines, then load more as the user scrolls (S4-R4). Paging never repeats or skips a customer, vendor or row, in any sort. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices, an open customer or vendor shows its first 100 documents, then the next 100 as the user scrolls; its document count, its subtotals, the Totals row and the exports always cover all of its documents.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 2 "Export" (board Export.dc.html); page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p2-export-menu-pdf-and-csv.png: figure "Export menu: PDF and CSV" (This build (after)), board "2. Export"
  • ar-ap-p7-past-due-ticked.png: figure "Past due ticked" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"

The design's own words:

  • "The native ⋯ Export menu on all six reports. Files hold exactly the rows on screen, in screen order, with the as-of date and locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor when chosen. S3-R1 to S3-R8, S3-R8a." (caption of "Export menu: PDF and CSV")
  • "31-60 days and 91+ days ticked: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" in blue. The Summary lists only customers with an amount in those ranges, at full balances; the Totals row adds up exactly these rows. S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18, S5-R19." (caption of "Past due ticked")
  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure the report has open documents in several buckets on today's date, one with more lines than fit on the screen.

cases.custom_steps:
1. Look at the table's top-left header cell.
  2. Look at each bucket row's own chevron.
  3. Hover over the top-left chevron button.
  4. Click it.
  5. Hover over it again.
  6. Scroll down through the tallest bucket.
  7. Switch ShopView to dark theme.
  8. Hover over the top-left chevron button.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • One chevron button, the design system's chevron icon, in the top-left header cell, pointing right (every group collapsed).

Step 2:

  • Every bucket row shows the same chevron, pointing right when closed.

Step 3:

  • A tooltip above the button reads "Expand all", letter for letter.

Step 4:

  • Every bucket opens and its chevron points down.

Step 5:

  • The tooltip above the button reads "Collapse all".

Step 6:

  • The bucket's row stays pinned just under the column headings, with its label visible at the left.

Step 7:

  • The page switches to dark theme.
  • The pinned row is readable.

Step 8:

  • The tooltip sits above the button and is readable in dark theme.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R1: “The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. When every group is collapsed it points right, its tooltip reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group.”
  • S4-R5: “Each group's own expand toggle uses the same chevron: pointing down when open, right when closed. Behavior is unchanged.”
  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

Expected Result

Step 1:

  • With date A as the as-of date, credit memo A is in "Current", not in "1-30 days past due" as before the feature was deployed on staging: from this release a credit dated exactly on the as-of date is Current.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 12 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • What changes for existing users: “A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit dated exactly on the as-of date now shows in Current with Past Due 0, as in QuickBooks; today it shows in 1-30 (S1-R5a).”
  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”

  6. Make invoice for customer C: Same way as invoice for customer A, on customer C's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid.   8. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make document A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 300.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 40 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, type 250.00 in the Payment box on this invoice's row, pick a Payment Method, then click Make Payment.
  3. Make customer B: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer B, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  4. Make document B: First set customer B's Credit Terms to "Due on Receipt" (edit icon beside the name, Edit Customer, Save), so this invoice falls due on its own date; set them back to "Net 30" right after. Same way as document A, on customer B's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type the date 20 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make customer C: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer C, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.

Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a new customer (created for this test), customer A, with open invoices on today's date of $1,250.50 that is 1 to 30 days past due and $99.00 that is more than 90 days past due, and nothing in the other buckets.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1250.50 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 45 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. Make invoice 2: Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 99.00; type the date 130 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure the report has open invoices, credit memos and deposits in at least three aging buckets on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group collapsed.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make invoice 2: Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type the date 45 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  4. Make invoice 3: Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 300.00; type the date 75 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make credit memo 1: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type the date 20 days before today in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  6. Make deposit 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Leave Invoice Date as today, click Create Invoice, and reload the page (F5) when the New Customer Payment window opens. The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.

In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 10.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. cases.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into customer A's rows.
  2. Keep scrolling until customer B's row reaches the top.
  3. Keep scrolling into customer B's rows.
  4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside customer A's rows again.
  5. Scroll down fast through customer A's and customer B's rows.
  6. Scroll fast back up through customer B's and customer A's rows.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • It shows the customer group's chevron (pointing down) and its label: customer A's name and count, then "Phone: " and the phone number and "Credit term: " and the credit term.
  • It shows no amounts (the customer group's sums stay in its own subtotal row).

Step 2:

  • Customer B's row pushes customer A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Customer B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: customer A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Step 6:

  • The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save.   3. Make invoice A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 500.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Step 5:

  • Location B is ticked again.

Step 6:

  • Location A is unticked.
  • The report narrows to location B.

Step 7:

  • Only credit memo A and deposit A remain.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. That is the location the Location column shows.”
  • Key Decisions, row location: “A row belongs to the location of its own open document (the invoice, credit memo or deposit; the bill or vendor credit), the same location the Location column shows. Rationale: the aging reports list open documents, not payments, so a partly paid invoice keeps its own location and the filter never contradicts the column. Rejected: splitting a balance by where each payment was taken.”
  • S6-R2: “The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.”

cases.title: A/P Detail: a vendor credit links to the return it came from
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations: your current location and your other location.
  • Have a vendor with three unused vendor credits: vendor credit A from a vendor return made at your current location, vendor credit B from a vendor return made at your other location, and vendor credit C not from a vendor return.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with that vendor ticked and its rows showing.

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type a new Name for vendor A, pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  3. Make bill 1: Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor. In Part Number type a new part number and click "Add new special order part: …"; type a Description, 1 in Quantity and 300.00 in Cost; click Add, then Save & Close. In the Purchase Orders list click Receive on that order (Vendor column: vendor A); type a Vendor Invoice # (for example bill 1), type today's date in Invoice Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Receive Parts (1).
  4. Make vendor credit A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return. Pick vendor A in Vendor, type a Packaging Slip, pick the part received on bill 1 in Part Number, type 40.00 in Price Per Unit, then click Save Return. In the Returns list tick that return and click Receive Credit; type a Credit Memo Number, type today's date in Credit Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Post Credit.
  5. Make bill 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as bill 1, with vendor A in Vendor: Cost 300.00; type today's date in Invoice Date.
  6. Make vendor credit B: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return. Pick vendor A in Vendor, type a Packaging Slip, pick the part received on bill 2 in Part Number, type 50.00 in Price Per Unit, then click Save Return. In the Returns list tick that return and click Receive Credit; type a Credit Memo Number, type today's date in Credit Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Post Credit.
  7. Make vendor credit C: Make vendor credit C for vendor A without a vendor return.

cases.title: A/R Detail: credit memos and deposits are plain text
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer with an unused credit memo A and an unused deposit A at your current location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with that customer ticked and every bucket expanded.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type today's date in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  3. Make deposit A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Leave Invoice Date as today, click Create Invoice, and reload the page (F5) when the New Customer Payment window opens. The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.

cases.title: Without Invoicing View, work order and part sale invoices are plain text
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as a user whose custom role has "Reports" in the Page Access card, "Work orders → View", "Part sales → View" (under the Parts Department switch) but not "Invoicing & payments → View".
  • Have a customer with an overdue work order invoice A and an overdue part sale invoice B, both made at your current location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with that customer's group expanded.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make work order invoice A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 300.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 45 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make part sale invoice B: Click Parts in the top bar, then Part Sales in the left menu, then New Part Sale; pick customer A in Customer and click Save. Click Add Part: in Part Number type a new part number and click "Add new special order part: …", type a Description, 1 in Quantity and a Cost, then click Save & Close; on the part's row type 300.00 in the Sell Price box. Click Authorize. On the part's row pick any Vendor and click Order (the status reads Awaiting), then click Receive on the row; tick the part, type a Vendor Invoice Number and click Receive Parts (1) (the status reads Received). Open the Finance tab, type the date 45 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice; reload the page when the New Customer Payment window opens.

In "Choose a template" click Skip (every switch then starts off). Type a Role Name, then switch on "Reports" in the Page Access card, tick View in the "Work orders" card, switch on Parts Department and tick View in "Part sales", and leave "Invoicing & payments" unticked, then click Create.
  5. Sign in with that role: Click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Settings, then Staff in the left menu. On the row "Tech ShopView" click the edit icon; in Edit Staff Member pick the new role in Role and click Save & Close. Then click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Logout, and on the QA site's sign-in page click Tech in the quick login panel. After the test, sign in as Admin again and set Tech ShopView's Role back to Technician.

  3. Make invoice 2: Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 1.00; type the date 31 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid.   8. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  9. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

Preconditions

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST Northern Alberta Heavy Haul and Towing Ltd (more than 40 characters), type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

Make invoice 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location column shows.
  • Have a customer with a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo, so the page shows a long name and a negative amount, which must not overlap or be cut off.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1536 px wide, in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST Northern Alberta Heavy Haul and Towing Ltd (more than 40 characters), type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  3. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  4. Make invoice 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make credit memo 1: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type today's date in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location column shows.
  • Have a customer with a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo, so the page shows a long name and a credit memo row, which must not overlap or be cut off.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1536 px wide, in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST Northern Alberta Heavy Haul and Towing Ltd (more than 40 characters), type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  3. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  4. Make invoice 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make credit memo 1: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type today's date in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.

On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer with an unused credit memo, credit memo A, and an unused deposit, deposit A, both dated the same earlier day, date A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with only that customer ticked in the Customer filter.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type the date 5 days before today in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  3. Make deposit A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Leave Invoice Date as today, click Create Invoice, and reload the page (F5) when the New Customer Payment window opens. The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.

cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report reloads for date A.

Step 2:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are listed in this bucket: a credit dated exactly on the as-of date is Current.

Step 3:

  • The report reloads for the day after date A, with every bucket collapsed.

Step 4:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are now listed here, one day past their own date, and no longer in "Current".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S4-N1: “Changing the as-of date, the customer or vendor filter, the Past due filter or the Location filter collapses every group, as changing the date or filter does today.”

Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice A: First set customer A's Credit Terms to "Due on Receipt" (edit icon beside the name, Edit Customer, Save), so this invoice falls due on its own date; set them back to "Net 30" right after. On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 300.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 10 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type the date 10 days before today in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  4. Make deposit A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.

cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a new customer (created for this test), customer A, with only these open documents on today's date: an invoice A of $500.00, 20 days past due, and an unused credit memo A of $120.00 dated today.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with only customer A ticked in the Customer filter.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 500.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 50 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type today's date in Credit Date, type 120.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
cases.custom_steps:
1. Read customer A's row and the Totals row.
  2. Open A/R Detail from the Reports menu.
  3. In the Customer filter, tick customer A.
  4. Click the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell (Expand all).
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Current $-120.00 and 1-30 Days $500.00; 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days and 91 And Over are blank.
  • Total $380.00 (500.00 − 120.00).
  • The Totals row reads the same: Current $-120.00, 1-30 Days $500.00, Total $380.00.

Step 2:

  • A/R Detail opens on today's date.

Step 3:

  • Customer A is ticked.

Step 4:

  • "Current" holds credit memo A with an Open Balance of $-120.00.
  • "1-30 days past due" holds invoice A with an Open Balance of $500.00.
