Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". cases.title: Design: A/R Customer menu keeps a long no-space name inside its row
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Create, for this test, a customer, customer A, whose name is 120 letters long with no spaces, and give them an open invoice dated today, so they are in the Customer menu.
  • Create, for this test, a second customer, customer B, whose name is more than 60 characters long and includes each of these characters: & " ' < >, and give them an open invoice dated today.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
cases.custom_steps:
1. Click the Customer chip.
  2. Scroll the list in the menu to customer A's row.
  3. Click customer A's tick box.
  4. Click the tick box in the row directly under customer A's row (if customer A's row is the last one, the row directly above it).
  5. Scroll the list to customer B's row.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Customer menu opens: a search box, "All customers", then the list of customers.

Step 2:

  • Customer A's whole name stays inside its own row (wrapped inside the row or shortened with "..."; either is a pass).
  • No part of it is drawn over the row under it or over that row's tick box; that row's name can be read.

Step 3:

  • Customer A is ticked.
  • The chip shows customer A's name, shortened with "...".

Step 4:

  • The customer in that row is ticked, and customer A stays ticked.
  • The chip reads "Customer: 2 customers".

Step 5:

  • Customer B's whole name, with its & " ' < > characters, stays inside its own row (wrapped inside the row or shortened with "..."; either is a pass).
  • No part of it is drawn over the row under it or over that row's tick box; that row's name can be read.

What you should see today: in step 2, customer A's name wraps onto about 4 lines; the first line is cut off at the top and the last line is drawn on top of the next customer's row and its tick box. The same happens in Sales By Customer's Customer menu. This is a known problem and it is already reported — see https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-12722 (filed 13 Nov 2026, after Demo Day).

· If you see exactly that, mark this test FAILED and do not raise anything new.

· If it fails in a DIFFERENT way from what is described above, that is a NEW problem — please report it.

· If it PASSES, the fix has shipped: report it so the ticket can be closed and this note removed.

cases.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
cases.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have two customers with open invoices on today's date, whose names differ only in capitals: customer A and customer B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST Capital Test, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make invoice for customer A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  3. Make customer B: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST CAPITAL TEST, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  4. Make invoice for customer B: Same way as invoice for customer A, on customer B's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
cases.custom_steps:
1. Find customer A and customer B in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
cases.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The two customers sit next to each other (no other customer between them) in one order.

Step 2:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 3:

  • The two names are in the same order as on screen.

Step 4:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 5:

  • The two rows are in the same order as on screen.

Step 6:

  • After the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. For example, "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing": the accent folds for the name order (S1-R3), so the two tie, and in the plain lower-cased name the unaccented letter comes first.”

Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".”

tests.title: A/R Detail: ID sorts by number value, and ties go by number
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that in the "1-30 days past due" bucket there are three open invoices with the same due date, document A, document B and document C, whose numbers have different digit counts, so that in number order they read document A, document B, document C but in letter-by-letter order document B, document C, document A.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Click the "ID" header.
  2. Click the "ID" header again.
  3. Click the "Due Date" header.
  4. Click the "Due Date" header again.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by ID as numbers, never letter by letter, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 2:

  • Largest number first: document C, document B, document A, still in number order.

Step 3:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by Due Date, oldest first.
  • Document A, document B and document C tie on Due Date, so they are ordered by number, smallest first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 4:

  • The Due Date sort reverses, newest first.
  • The three still tie and keep the same order, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C (reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only).

  • S3-R4: “Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).”

  • S3-R8: “The CSV starts with the lines of S3-R5, each in its own row, in this order: As of, Locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor line only when set. tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and your other location.
  • Make sure vendor A and vendor B each have bills at location A that were 31 to 60 and more than 90 days past due on Oct 15, 2026.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the as-of date set to 10/15/2026 and only location A ticked in the Location filter (the Location column is hidden).
tests.custom_steps:
1. In the Past due filter, tick "91+ days", then "31-60 days".
  2. In the Vendor filter, tick vendor B, then vendor A.
  3. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  4. Open the PDF and read the lines under its title.
  5. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  6. Open the CSV and read the lines at the top.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Both ranges are ticked.

Step 2:

  • Both vendors are ticked.
  • The chip reads "Vendor: 2 vendors".

Step 3:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 4:

  • The lines read "As of Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days" (menu order, not the order ticked), then "Vendors: " and vendor B, vendor A (the order ticked).
  • The PDF has no Location column.

Step 5:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 6:

  • The CSV starts with four rows of one line each, in this order: "As of: Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days", then "Vendors: " and vendor B, vendor A.
  • The column heading row follows directly.
  • There is no Location column.

  • S3-R4: “Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).”

Under it, only when set: "Past due: " and the ticked ranges in menu order (for example "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days"), then, for one ticked customer or vendor, "Customer: " or "Vendor: " and the name, and for several, "Customers: " or "Vendors: " and the names in the order they were ticked.”
  • S3-R8: “The CSV starts with the lines of S3-R5, each in its own row, in this order: As of, Locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor line only when set. The column heading row follows directly, then one flat table: one row per customer or vendor (Summaries) or per document (Detail, Collection, Unpaid Invoices), with the aging bucket, customer or vendor in its own column; no group header or subtotal rows; one Totals row at the bottom. Money is a plain number with two decimals, and an empty bucket is a blank cell; dates are YYYY-MM-DD.”

(or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location filter shows and can be cleared.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open the Location filter.
  2. Click "Clear selection".
  3. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Location menu opens.

Step 2:

  • No location is ticked.
  • The empty state shows, with a "Clear all filters" button, no totals and no Location column.

Step 3:

  • The warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results" shows.
  • Nothing is downloaded (no new file in the browser's downloads).

Step 4:

  • The same warning shows.
  • Nothing is downloaded.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”
  • S5-R6a: “With no location ticked ("Clear selection" or unticking every row), the report shows no rows: the native empty state (S8-R5) with "Clear all filters", no totals and no Location column. An export from that state downloads nothing and shows "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results", as on Sales By Customer.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export with no rows | "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results" | Warning toast; nothing downloads”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html). Design pictures attached to this case:

The design's own words:

  • ""Clear selection" leaves no location chosen: the chip reads "Location: No locations" and stays visible, and the table shows the native empty state "No record matches these filters" with "Clear all filters". No Totals row and no Location column. Reshot 2026-10-23 (round 15). S5-R6a, S5-R9." (caption of "Cleared: No locations")

tests.title: A/R Detail: a CSV export that fails shows one error and downloads nothing
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer with an open invoice on today's date, so the report has rows.
  • Make sure you can switch this computer's network connection off and on (such as Wi-Fi).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Switch the computer's network connection off.
  2. Click the ⋯ button.
  3. Click "Download (CSV)".
  4. Switch the network connection back on.
  5. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The computer is offline.
  • The report stays on screen.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • The error message "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." shows: exactly one message, no second generic error.
  • Nothing is downloaded (no new file in the browser's downloads).

Step 4:

  • The connection is back.

Step 5:

  • The CSV downloads: a new export works again.

The server-error half of the same sentence cannot be caused by hand; the developers' automated tests cover it. This case covers the lost connection.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • Story 3, Error Handling: “If an export fails for any other reason (a server error or a lost connection), nothing downloads and one error message shows: "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." This message is on these six reports only; the other reports keep theirs.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export fails for any other reason | "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." | Error toast; nothing downloads; these six reports only”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 2 "Export" (board Export.dc.html). The design draws no picture of this behaviour (all 7 boards and 45 figures checked); the case follows the PRD.

tests.title: A/R Detail: exporting with every bucket closed still downloads every row
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer, customer A, with three open invoices on today's date, in two different aging buckets.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the Customer filter showing only customer A ticked.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Click the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell until its tooltip reads "Expand all" (every bucket closed).
  2. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the CSV and read its rows.
  4. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the PDF and read its rows.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Every bucket is closed: no document row shows on screen.

Step 2:

  • The CSV downloads with the "Success" message "Data exported successfully."
  • No "Empty export" warning shows.

Step 3:

  • One row for each of customer A's three invoices, then the Totals row: the same rows the report has with its buckets open.

Step 4:

  • The PDF downloads with the "Success" message.

Step 5:

  • The same three invoices and the Totals row.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S3-R3: “The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D28, rationale: “On Detail reports with every bucket collapsed no rows are loaded, so a loaded-rows check would wrongly say "Empty export" (S3-R10).”
  • Tech plan §3 D28: “Empty-export detection reads the report's server count, never loaded rows: Summaries pagination.rowsNumber; Collection/Unpaid totals.documentCount; Detail totals.rowsNumber from the groups query”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 2 "Export" (board Export.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD and tech plan quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p2-export-menu-pdf-and-csv.png: figure "Export menu: PDF and CSV" (This build (after)), board "2. Export"

The design's own words:

  • "The native ⋯ Export menu on all six reports. Files hold exactly the rows on screen, in screen order, with the as-of date and locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor when chosen. S3-R1 to S3-R8, S3-R8a." (caption of "Export menu: PDF and CSV")

tests.title: A/R Summary: a name starting with = opens in the CSV as plain text
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer, customer A, with an open invoice on today's date, and its name starts with "=" so that it reads like a spreadsheet formula.
  • Make sure a spreadsheet program is installed on the computer.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the Customer filter showing only customer A ticked.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Read customer A's name on screen.
  2. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the CSV in the spreadsheet program.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The name shows as it was typed, starting with "=".

Step 2:

  • The CSV downloads with the "Success" message.

Step 3:

  • The spreadsheet opens the file, and customer A's name cell shows the name's own characters as text (a mark may be added in front of them so the spreadsheet keeps them as text).
  • It does not show a calculated number (such as 5) or an error (such as #NAME?).

Why: a name that a spreadsheet would run as a formula is a known risk in exported files; the tech plan says the CSV guards against it.

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §9 Security: “CSV formula-injection hardening via CsvAttachmentResponseBuilder (system numeric columns masked as safe).”

tests.title: A/R Collection: the top-left chevron collapses and expands every group
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that at least three customers have overdue invoices on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group collapsed.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Click the chevron on one customer group row.
  2. Hover over the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell.
  3. Click that chevron button.
  4. Hover over the chevron button again.
  5. Click it.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • That customer group expands.
  • Its own chevron turns from pointing right to pointing down.

Step 2:

  • The button's chevron points down (a group is expanded).
  • A tooltip above the button reads "Collapse all".

Step 3:

  • Every group collapses.
  • The column under the button was not sorted: the sort mark is still on the column the report opened on.

Step 4:

  • The chevron now points right.
  • The tooltip reads "Expand all".

Step 5:

  • Every group expands.
  • The column under the button is still not sorted.
  • Every customer group row's own chevron points down (open).

This release does not change how the groups open, so they open as today; the starting screen asks for every group collapsed, collapsing any that are open.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R1: “The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. When every group is collapsed it points right, its tooltip reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group.”
  • S4-R3: “Clicking the button never sorts the column under it.”
  • S4-R5: “Each group's own expand toggle uses the same chevron: pointing down when open, right when closed. Behavior is unchanged.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Collapse all / Expand all button | "Collapse all" / "Expand all" | Tooltip above the button”

  5. Scroll down fast through bucket A's and bucket B's rows.

tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Bucket A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • It shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count.
  • It shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row).

Step 2:

  • Bucket B's row pushes bucket A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Bucket B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: bucket A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Step 6:

  • The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

tests.title: A/R Summary: the filter row reads As of, Customer, Past due, Location
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location chip shows.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps: 1. Read the filter row under the title, chip by chip, left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Four chips, in this order: the date chip "As of: " and today's date (for example "As of: 10/15/2026"), the Customer chip, the Past due chip, the Location chip.
  • The date chip says "As of", no longer "Date".
  • The Customer chip reads "Customer: All customers" with a person icon.
  • The Past due chip reads "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon.
  • Both are in the resting (grey) style.
  • The Location chip reads "Location: All locations" with the location pin icon.
  • Every label matches exactly, capitals and punctuation included.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S5-R6: “The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.”
  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”
  • S5-R10a: “Filter choices are not remembered between visits: opening a report from the Reports menu starts on today's as-of date, no customer or vendor, Past due Any, and All locations.”
  • What changes for existing users: “The date filter is labelled "As of" (was "Date"). On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices the Customer or Vendor chip now comes after it.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html).   • ar-ap-p7-past-due-ticked.png: figure "Past due ticked" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Summary: date only" (Production (before)), board "7. Filters and call list" (today's look, for comparison only)

  • "The native checkbox menu: "Any" ticked, "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then 1-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 91+ days. S5-R15, S5-N3." (caption of "Past due menu")
  • "31-60 days and 91+ days ticked: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" in blue. The Summary lists only customers with an amount in those ranges, at full balances; the Totals row adds up exactly these rows. S5-R15, S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18, S5-R19." (caption of "Past due ticked")

tests.custom_steps: 1. Read the filter row under the title, chip by chip, left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Four chips, in this order: the date chip "As of: " and today's date (for example "As of: 10/15/2026"), the Vendor chip, the Past due chip, the Location chip.
  • The date chip says "As of", no longer "Date".
  • The Vendor chip reads "Vendor: All vendors" with a truck icon.
  • The Past due chip reads "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon.
  • Both are in the resting (grey) style.
  • The Location chip reads "Location: All locations" with the location pin icon.
  • Every label matches exactly, capitals and punctuation included.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S5-R6: “The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.”
  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”

tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

tests.title: A/R Collection: a link with an unknown customer ignores it
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer, customer A, with overdue invoices on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. In the Customer filter, tick customer A.
  2. In the address bar, after customer A's code (the text after "customerIds="), add a comma and "Nobody".
  3. Press Enter.
  4. In the address bar, replace everything after "customerIds=" with "Nobody".
  5. Press Enter.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The chip reads "Customer: " and customer A's name.
  • Only customer A's group is listed.
  • The page address carries "customerIds=" followed by customer A's code (a long code, not the name).

Step 2:

  • The address bar shows customer A's code, a comma and "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

Step 3:

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: " and customer A's name.
  • Only customer A's group is listed: the unknown customer is ignored.

Step 4:

  • The address bar shows "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

Step 5:

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: All customers" in the resting (grey) style: with no known customer left, the link opens as if none were ticked.

Why: a link saved earlier can name a customer that was since deleted or merged; the tech plan says such a link must still open the report.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R19: “The ticked customers or vendors and the ticked Past due ranges are kept in the page address like Location (S5-R10).”
  • S5-R14: “A customer or vendor ticked through a link, a reload or a Summary drill-down is named and ticked on the chip, even when it is not among the first results of the chip's search.”

tests.title: A/R Collection: a report that fails to load says so in place of the rows
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Use Google Chrome (or Microsoft Edge) on a desktop: the report's data is cut off with the browser's own blocking tool. Switching Wi-Fi off does not work for this test: ShopView then sends nothing, waits for the connection and shows no message (as before this release).
  • Run it on staging. On a QA site the page shows the result for about 5 seconds, then the site's own "QA env is sleeping" notice moves it to an "Environment Sleeping" page, so only the first steps can be judged there.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Block the report's data: press F12, click the ⋮ menu at the top right of the panel that opens, choose More tools, then Network request blocking; tick "Enable network request blocking", click +, type *reporting/reports* and click Add. Leave the panel open.
  2. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
  3. Unblock it: in the Network request blocking panel, untick "Enable network request blocking".
  4. Change the as-of date back to today.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The computer is offline.

Step 2:

  • The report tries to load and fails: in place of the rows it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again.", with the standard error message as well.

Step 3:

  • The computer is online again.

Step 4:

  • The report loads normally again.


A server error cannot be caused by hand; a lost connection is the failure a tester can cause.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R6: “If a report fails to load, it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, with the standard error message.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Report fails to load | "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." | In place of the rows, plus the standard error toast”

tests.title: A/R Summary: 30 customers at a time, none repeated or skipped
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that between 31 and 90 customers have open documents on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  2. Open the CSV and count the customers in it (each name once).
  3. Count the customers shown before any more load (or compare them with the first 30 names in the CSV) and note the last one.
  4. Scroll down until the next customers load.
  5. Keep scrolling to the end of the list, writing down each customer's name.
  6. Click the "Total" header.
  7. Scroll from the top to the end of the list again, writing down each name.
  8. In the Past due filter, tick "1-30 days".
  9. Tick "91+ days".
  10. Scroll from the top to the end of the list again, writing down each name.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 2:

  • Note the number of customers (for example 46).

Step 3:

  • Exactly 30 customers.

Step 4:

  • The next customers load below as you scroll (there are no page buttons), starting with the customer that comes right after the last one noted in step 3, not a repeat.

Step 5:

  • Every customer appears exactly once and the count equals the CSV's.

Step 6:

  • The rows sort by Total, largest first.

Step 7:

  • In this sort too, every customer appears exactly once and none is missing.

Step 8:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 1-30 days" and the report reloads with that range only.

Step 9:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" and the report reloads with both ranges.

Step 10:

  • Every customer left by the filter appears exactly once.
  • None repeats as more load.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today.   • What changes for existing users: “A/R reports no longer come out in an unpredictable order; A/R Summary and A/R Collection no longer repeat or skip customers between pages.”

tests.title: Design: A/R Summary loading bar and empty state match Sales By Customer
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with open invoices only at location B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Change the as-of date to yesterday and watch the table straight away.
  2. Change the as-of date back to today.
  3. In the Location menu, untick location B.
  4. In the Customer filter, tick customer A.
  5. Read the empty state, letter for letter, and compare it with Sales By Customer's empty state.
  6. Click "Clear all filters".
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A progress bar shows on the table while the report loads, the same loading bar Sales By Customer shows.

Step 2:

  • The report shows today again.

Step 3:

  • The report narrows to location A.

Step 4:

  • The report has no rows: customer A has nothing open at location A.

Step 5:

  • "No record matches these filters" and "Try changing filters to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button, laid out the same as Sales By Customer's empty state when the two tabs are compared.
  • No Totals row.

Step 6:

  • The filters return to their defaults and rows show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R5: “While a report loads it shows the native table progress bar. When the filters leave no rows, it shows the native empty state: "No record matches these filters" and "Try changing filters to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button when a customer or vendor, Past due or Location is chosen; that button keeps the as-of date and returns the customer or vendor, Past due and Location to their defaults (every location ticked).”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Filters leave no rows | "No record matches these filters", "Try changing filters to widen your results." | Native empty state with "Clear all filters"”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html). The design pictures one empty state (No locations on A/R Detail); the loading bar is not drawn.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p4-cleared-no-locations-reshot-2026-11-05.png: figure "Cleared: No locations" (This build (after)), board "4. Location filter and Location column", re-shot 23 Oct 2026, design version of 5 Nov 2026

The design's own words:

  • ""Clear selection" leaves no location chosen: the chip reads "Location: No locations" and stays visible, and the table shows the native empty state "No record matches these filters" with "Clear all filters". No Totals row and no Location column. Reshot 2026-10-23 (round 15). S5-R6a, S5-R9." (caption of "Cleared: No locations")

The design version of 5 Nov 2026 replaced the picture "Cleared: No locations" (re-shot 23 Oct 2026): compare with ar-ap-p4-cleared-no-locations-reshot-2026-11-05.png only. tests.title: Design: A/R Detail chevron button, tooltips and pinned group row
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure the report has open documents in several buckets on today's date, one with more lines than fit on the screen.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group collapsed.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Look at the table's top-left header cell.
  2. Look at each bucket row's own chevron.
  3. Hover over the top-left chevron button.
  4. Click it.
  5. Hover over it again.
  6. Scroll down through the tallest bucket.
  7. Switch ShopView to dark theme.
  8. Hover over the top-left chevron button.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • One chevron button, the design system's chevron icon, in the top-left header cell, pointing right (every group collapsed).

Step 2:

  • Every bucket row shows the same chevron, pointing right when closed.

Step 3:

  • A tooltip above the button reads "Expand all", letter for letter.

Step 4:

  • Every bucket opens and its chevron points down.

Step 5:

  • The tooltip above the button reads "Collapse all".

Step 6:

  • The bucket's row stays pinned just under the column headings, with its label visible at the left.

Step 7:

  • The page switches to dark theme.
  • The pinned row is readable.

Step 8:

  • The tooltip sits above the button and is readable in dark theme.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S4-R1: “The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. When every group is collapsed it points right, its tooltip reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group.”
  • S4-R5: “Each group's own expand toggle uses the same chevron: pointing down when open, right when closed. Behavior is unchanged.”
  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Collapse all / Expand all button | "Collapse all" / "Expand all" | Tooltip above the button”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 3 "Collapse all and pinned group rows" (board Grouped.dc.html); page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html); page 5 "Document links and Switch location" (board Links.dc.html). The design shows the chevrons on A/R Detail but no picture of the Collapse all / Expand all tooltip.

  • ar-ap-p5-links-only-where-they-can-open-reshot-2026-11-05.png: figure "Links only where they can open" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)", re-shot 23 Oct 2026, design version of 5 Nov 2026
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-collection-date-and-customer-only.png: figure "A/R Collection, groups opened one by one" (Production (before)), board "3. Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows" (today's look, for comparison only)

tests.title: Design: A/R Summary load error message shows in place of the rows
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a customer with an open invoice on today's date, so the report has rows.
  • Use Google Chrome (or Microsoft Edge) on a desktop: the report's data is cut off with the browser's own blocking tool. Switching Wi-Fi off does not work for this test: ShopView then sends nothing, waits for the connection and shows no message (as before this release).
  • Run it on staging. On a QA site the page shows the result for about 5 seconds, then the site's own "QA env is sleeping" notice moves it to an "Environment Sleeping" page, so only the first steps can be judged there.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Block the report's data: press F12, click the ⋮ menu at the top right of the panel that opens, choose More tools, then Network request blocking; tick "Enable network request blocking", click +, type *reporting/reports* and click Add. Leave the panel open.
  2. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
  3. Unblock it: in the Network request blocking panel, untick "Enable network request blocking".
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The computer is offline.

Step 2:

  • The report fails to load: "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." shows in place of the rows.
  • The standard error message shows as well.

Step 3:

  • The connection is back.


Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R6: “If a report fails to load, it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, with the standard error message.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Report fails to load | "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." | In place of the rows, plus the standard error toast”

Last checked against build v26.45.2-6a8b89c (QA site sv11315) on 11/10/2026.


References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 6 "Descriptions and pinned column" (board Layout.dc.html). The design draws no load error (all 7 boards checked); the case follows the PRD.

tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure that in the "1-30 days past due" bucket there are three open invoices, document A, document B and document C, each for a different customer, so the rows sort across customers:
  • Document A is dated 40 days ago, due 10 days ago, amount $300.00, open $50.00.
  • Document B is dated 20 days ago, due 20 days ago, amount $100.00, open $100.00.
  • Document C is dated 35 days ago, due 5 days ago, amount $200.00, open $150.00.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make document A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 300.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 40 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, type 250.00 in the Payment box on this invoice's row, pick a Payment Method, then click Make Payment.
  3. Make customer B: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer B, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  4. Make document B: First set customer B's Credit Terms to "Due on Receipt" (edit icon beside the name, Edit Customer, Save), so this invoice falls due on its own date; set them back to "Net 30" right after. Same way as document A, on customer B's page: Fixed Line Total 100.00; type the date 20 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make customer C: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer C, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  6. Make document C: Same way as document A, on customer C's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type the date 35 days before today in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window type 50.00 in the Payment box on this invoice's row, pick a Payment Method, then click Make Payment.

tests.custom_preconds:

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make document A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 300.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type the date 40 days before today in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).

Setup

  1. Make vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type a new Name for vendor A, pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  2. Make bill 1: Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor.   4. Make bill 3: Same way as bill 1, with vendor A in Vendor: Cost 300.00; type the date 40 days before today in Invoice Date.

  6. Make vendor credit 1: Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return. Pick vendor A in Vendor, type a Packaging Slip, pick the part received on bill 1 in Part Number, type 60.00 in Price Per Unit, then click Save Return. In the Returns list tick that return and click Receive Credit; type a Credit Memo Number, type the date 40 days before today in Credit Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Post Credit.

tests.title: A/R Summary: the sort stays while changing date, scrolling and filters
tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Make sure the report has more than 30 customers with open documents on today's date and on yesterday's date, at both locations.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with open documents at both locations.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  3. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  4. Make invoice 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.

Step 6:

  • "Total" is still marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R7: “The sort is kept while the user stays on the report: changing the as-of date, loading more rows by scrolling, and changing the customer, vendor, Past due or Location filter keep it, except as in S2-R7a.”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”
  • S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. There are no page buttons. A/R Detail and A/P Detail show each bucket's first 100 lines, then load more as the user scrolls (S4-R4). Paging never repeats or skips a customer, vendor or row, in any sort. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices, an open customer or vendor shows its first 100 documents, then the next 100 as the user scrolls; its document count, its subtotals, the Totals row and the exports always cover all of its documents.”

  • Leave the report with the Vendor filter showing vendor A ticked and its group expanded.

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make vendor A: Click Parts in the top bar, then Vendors in the left menu, then New Vendor. Type a new Name for vendor A, pick Credit Terms "Net 30" and Taxes "Exempt (0%)", then click Save & Close.
  3. Make bill 1: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Click Parts in the top bar, then Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO. Pick vendor A in Vendor. In the Purchase Orders list click Receive on that order (Vendor column: vendor A); type a Vendor Invoice # (for example bill 1), type today's date in Invoice Date, type 0 in Tax, then click Receive Parts (1).
  4. Make vendor credit A: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Click Parts in the top bar, then Returns in the left menu, then Create Return.   • Customer C's $900.00 is gone.

Step 8:

  • The CSV downloads.

  • The CSV's Totals row reads $550.00, the same as the screen.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S5-R16: “With ranges ticked, A/R Detail, A/R Collection, A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices keep only the invoices and bills whose days past due on the as-of date fall in a ticked range, and always keep credit memos, deposits and vendor credits.”
  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. tests.custom_steps:
1. In the Vendor filter, tick vendor A and vendor B.
  2. In the Past due filter, tick "31-60 days".
  3. Expand every group and read the rows and the Totals row.
  4. In the Location filter, untick location B.
  5. Expand every group and read the rows and the Totals row.
  6. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.

  8. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.

tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Only the two vendors' documents remain.
  • Vendor C's $900.00 is gone.
  • The Totals row's Open Balance reads $2,200.00 (1,000.00 + 400.00 − 150.00 + 700.00 + 250.00): the Totals row follows the vendor filter.

Step 2:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 31-60 days".

Step 3:

  • The rows are the $400.00 and $700.00 documents (45 days past due) and the $150.00 vendor credit, which is always kept.
  • The Totals row reads $950.00 (400.00 + 700.00 − 150.00).

Step 4:

  • The report narrows to location A.

Step 5:

  • The rows are the $700.00 document and the $150.00 vendor credit.
  • The Totals row reads $550.00 (700.00 − 150.00).

Step 6:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 7:

  • The PDF's Totals row reads $550.00, the same as the screen.

Step 8:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 9:

  • The CSV's Totals row reads $550.00, the same as the screen.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S5-R16: “With ranges ticked, A/R Detail, A/R Collection, A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices keep only the invoices and bills whose days past due on the as-of date fall in a ticked range, and always keep credit memos, deposits and vendor credits.”
  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. That is the location the Location column shows.”

tests.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, in dark theme at 100% zoom.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with every group expanded (Expand all).
  • Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab, also in dark theme, for comparison.

Setup

  1. Locations to use: Use "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" as location A (it comes first in A to Z order) and "Staging Lethbridge - 4310" as location B. To work at location B, click the location name and your initials at the top right of the top bar, then Change Location, then "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"; switch back to "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" the same way when you are done.
  2. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type the Name ZZAUTOTEST Northern Alberta Heavy Haul and Towing Ltd (more than 40 characters), type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  3. Make invoice 1: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, then click Save (click Ok if a Customer Notes window opens). In the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 100.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Type today's date in Invoice Date, then click Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment window opens, reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  4. Make invoice 2: While switched to location B (see the Locations to use item): Same way as invoice 1, on customer A's page: Fixed Line Total 200.00; type today's date in Invoice Date; then in the New Customer Payment window reload the page (F5) so the invoice stays unpaid. Do not close that window with its ×: that takes the new invoice away again.
  5. Make credit memo 1: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type today's date in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.

(or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).

Setup

  1. Make customer A: Click Customers in the top bar, then New Customer. Type a new Name for customer A, type a Phone, then click Save. On the customer's page click the edit icon beside the name; in Edit Customer pick Credit Terms "Net 30", pick Taxes "Exempt (0%)" and type 0 in Default Shop Supplies (so totals stay exact), then click Save. Click Add Contact, type a First name and Last name, then click Save. On the Assets tab click New Asset, pick the Contact, fill Make and the other boxes the window marks as required, then click Save.
  2. Make credit memo A: On customer A's page open the Invoices tab and click Issue Credit. Type the date 5 days before today in Credit Date, type 50.00 in Amount, click Issue Store Credit (not Issue Refund), type a Reason, then click Issue Credit.
  3. Make deposit A: On customer A's page click New Work Order, pick the Asset, click Save, and close the New Line window. Open the Finance tab and click Add Deposit; in Create Deposit pick a Payment Method and type 41.00 in Deposit Amount, then click Record Deposit. Open the Lines tab and click New Line; in the New Line window type a Title, pick Labor Rate "Fixed Line Total" (type "Fixed" in the box to find it), type 1.00 in Fixed Line Total, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the line click Complete; in Tech stories type a story and click Complete All Lines (if Missing Details asks for Mileage, type it and click Complete All Lines again). Open the Finance tab and click Mark Reviewed (if a window asks for the VIN, type one and click Confirm Review). Leave Invoice Date as today, click Create Invoice, and reload the page (F5) when the New Customer Payment window opens. The invoice is paid from the deposit, and the rest, 40.00, stays as an unused deposit dated today.

1. Change the as-of date to date A.
  2. Expand the "Current" bucket.
  3. Change the as-of date to the day after date A.
  4. Expand the "1-30 days past due" bucket.
tests.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report reloads for date A.

Step 2:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are listed in this bucket: a credit dated exactly on the as-of date is Current.

Step 3:

  • The report reloads for the day after date A, with every bucket collapsed.

Step 4:

  • Credit memo A and deposit A are now listed here, one day past their own date, and no longer in "Current".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S4-N1: “Changing the as-of date, the customer or vendor filter, the Past due filter or the Location filter collapses every group, as changing the date or filter does today.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S5-R18a: “For the same as-of date, customer or vendor and Location, with Past due on Any, A/R Summary's Totals equal A/R Detail's Open Balance Totals bucket by bucket, and A/P Summary's equal A/P Detail's. The Detail reports' Amount column holds original amounts and is not compared. With a Past due filter they can differ: a Summary keeps the whole row of a customer or vendor that qualifies (Current and credits included), while a Detail report lists only the invoices or bills that qualify, plus every credit.”
  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”

Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • Step 4 (our restatement, not the PRD's words): The credit memo dated today is under "Current" (production put it in "1-30 days past due").

This case checks the same planned change from the before-the-release side.

Why this matters: Only the same-day credit was meant to move; older credits must age as before.
